title: Space Tech Briefing — July 26, 2026
summary:
Good morning, space enthusiasts! It's Saturday, July 26, 2026, and we are kicking off your weekend with some absolutely stellar news from the cosmos! Get ready for a high-energy dive into the latest and greatest in space technology.

Let's blast off with the biggest news of the past 24 hours! SpaceX has just achieved a monumental success with its 13th Starship test flight! Taking off on July 24th UTC, this mission confirmed several major technical objectives. We saw the deployment of the very first Starlink V3 satellites, a critical in-flight engine relight, and a flawless atmospheric re-entry of the upper stage, culminating in a gentle splashdown in the Indian Ocean. This flight marks a significant step forward for the Starship program, definitively validating the Raptor V3 engines in space. The question now on everyone's lips is: will the 14th flight be the one for a first orbital attempt? We're certainly watching that space!

And as we celebrate those incredible advancements, let's take a moment to look back at a fascinating development that has recently captured our attention in the world of space agriculture. Remember the incredible work of astronaut Sophie Adenot aboard the International Space Station? She's been busy with the ChlorISS experiment, successfully growing plants in microgravity! It's a vital step for long-duration space missions, pushing the boundaries of what's possible for human survival beyond Earth. But while her current work is groundbreaking, it also reminds us that humanity's green thumb in space has a rich and enduring history.

What an incredible morning for space exploration! From the next-generation Starship pushing the limits of launch capabilities to the enduring quest for sustainable life support with space agriculture, the future is truly blossoming. That's all for now, but keep looking up! This has been your space technology briefing. Have a fantastic weekend!
